title: Lake Fyans, Grampians National Park, Victoria, Australia
caption: A reservoir of reflections
subtitle: Lake Fyans, Grampians National Park, Victoria, Australia
description:
At first glance, today's image looks more like a drowned woodland than a lake. Bare tree trunks emerge from the water, their reflections stretching across the surface as the Grampians glow in the distance. This is Lake Fyans, a man-made off-stream reservoir at the foot of the Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park in Victoria, Australia. Part of the regional Wimmera-Mallee water supply system, it also draws anglers with its brown and rainbow trout and trophy-sized redfin.
The mountains beyond the lake are part of the Grampians, a range shaped over hundreds of millions of years. Today, the region is known for rugged sandstone peaks, dramatic lookouts, waterfalls and rich Aboriginal cultural heritage. On the water, visitors can sail, kayak, jet-ski and water-ski, while trails through the surrounding landscape offer encounters with kangaroos, emus and native birds.
Lake Fyans captures that wild spirit in a single scene: flooded trees, open skies and an ever-changing backdrop of ancient mountains.

title: Old Town Hall, Bamberg, Germany
caption: Where history flows along the canal
subtitle: Old Town Hall, Bamberg, Germany
description:
Perched above the Regnitz River, Bamberg's Old Town Hall is one of Germany's most distinctive landmarks. According to local legend, the town's bishop refused to give citizens land for their town hall, so they created their own artificial island in the river by driving wooden piles into the riverbed. The building that rose there became a symbol of civic independence and remains one of Bavaria's most photographed scenes.
The Old Town Hall blends Gothic and Baroque elements, but its colourful exterior holds an even bigger surprise. Elaborate trompe-l'œil frescoes create the illusion of columns, shadows and architectural details, while a mischievous cherub appears to poke a three-dimensional leg through the painted wall. The historic Upper Bridge also passes directly through the building, allowing pedestrians to walk through it as they cross the river.
Inside, the ornate Rococo Hall and the Ludwig Collection of European porcelain add another layer to the landmark's rich cultural story, making the Old Town Hall as fascinating up close as it is from the river.

title: Beech tree in a cereal field, East Meon, South Downs National Park, Hampshire, England
caption: Fields of gold
subtitle: Beech tree in a cereal field, Hampshire, England
description:
A beech tree stands alone amid golden fields near East Meon in Hampshire, providing a striking focal point in the rolling landscape of England's South Downs National Park. Agriculture has shaped these chalk hills for centuries, and farming remains an important part of the region today. The area's free-draining chalk soils support extensive arable farming, with wheat and barley among the most common crops. Throughout the summer, these crops ripen in the fields before harvest transforms the countryside into a patchwork of gold and stubble.
Early September coincides with the main harvest season, when rural communities begin celebrating the year's bounty. In villages such as East Meon, harvest traditions remain an enduring part of local life, reflecting the deep connection between the land and the people who work it. Framed by open skies and sweeping farmland, this solitary tree stands as a symbol of the South Downs' long agricultural heritage.

title: Gabit Keni Beach near Ankola, Karnataka, India
caption: Life on India's west coast
subtitle: Gabit Keni Beach near Ankola, Karnataka, India
description:
When people think of South India, they often picture spice routes, classical music, folk traditions and a coastline shaped by centuries of maritime life. Follow Karnataka's Arabian Sea coast to the quieter shores of Gabit Keni Beach near Ankola, where fishing remains part of everyday life.
The beach is named after the Gabit fishing community. It's an easy stop while exploring the Uttara Kannada district, especially alongside Gokarna, Karwar and the historic Mirjan Fort. It also has an unusual landmark just offshore: a rocky island topped by the Sri Mangteshwar Temple. A path of large rocks crosses the water, providing access to the temple when sea conditions permit. The setting has earned comparisons with Bali's famous Tanah Lot, although Gabit Keni remains far less developed and crowded.
The surrounding Ankola region is known for its fishing communities, cashews and Ishaad mangoes. Nearby Gokarna, Karwar and Mirjan Fort make the beach an easy addition to a coastal Karnataka itinerary.

title: Aerial view of Olvera, Andalusia, Spain
caption: A patchwork from above
subtitle: Aerial view of Olvera, Andalusia, Spain
description:
Ever wondered why Andalusia is one of Spain's best-known regions? Flamenco, tapas, Moorish architecture and extensive olive groves all play a part. Beyond its famous cities, you'll find historic places like Olvera. Surrounded by more than 2 million olive trees, this village developed as a strategic frontier settlement shaped by centuries of change. The Castle of Olvera still watches over the town, while the Church of Our Lady of the Incarnation dominates the skyline below. Visit La Cilla Cultural Center to discover Olvera's medieval history and traditions.
Hungry? Try 'gazpacho,' a chilled tomato soup; 'jamón ibérico,' Spain's famous cured ham or the 'torta de aceite,' a crisp olive oil biscuit. For a scenic walk or bike ride, head to the Vía Verde de la Sierra, a former railway line turned popular trail. Watch your step on the steep cobbled streets—your camera might stay steady, but your footing may not! As the saying goes, 'poco a poco'—little by little. Slow down, wander and let Olvera reveal itself.

title: The bay of Villefranche-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
caption: Where the Mediterranean reigns supreme
subtitle: Villefranche-sur-Mer, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
description:
In September, the French Riviera is bathed in softer light, and the Mediterranean vegetation begins to regain its vibrancy. Along the coast, rosemary, wild thyme and Aleppo pine scent the air, while sailboats drift across the sheltered waters of Villefranche-sur-Mer.
The town's spectacular bay is one of the deepest natural harbours in the Mediterranean, allowing large ships to anchor close to shore. Above the waterfront, pastel-coloured buildings climb the hills, while the 16th-century Fort Saint-Elme stands as a reminder of the town's strategic past. Wander through the old streets and you can discover Rue Obscure, a covered medieval passageway once used for defence and shelter.
Villefranche-sur-Mer has also inspired artists and filmmakers. Jean Cocteau transformed the Chapel of Saint Peter in 1957, covering its interior with colourful murals celebrating the lives of local fishermen. With its deep blue waters, historic streets and Mediterranean vegetation, the town blends natural beauty, heritage and Riviera charm.

title: Interior of the Royal Albert Hall, London
caption: A finale worth singing about
subtitle: Last Night of the Proms
description:
What happens when a grand classical concert lets its hair down? The Last Night of the Proms. The finale of the annual BBC Proms turns London's Royal Albert Hall into a joyful, flag-waving party, where world-class music meets quirky costumes, inflatable toys and enthusiastic singalongs.
The Proms began in 1895, and the Last Night gradually developed its distinctive traditions. Today, Prommers arrive waving Union Jacks and other flags, wearing everything from flag-covered suits to Viking helmets, and occasionally brandishing inflatable bananas or squeaky ducks. A traditional favourite, Henry Wood's 'Fantasia on British Sea-Songs' often gets the crowd stamping and whistling, while favourites including 'Jerusalem,' 'Rule, Britannia!' and Elgar's 'Land of Hope and Glory' turn the finale into one enormous chorus.
Getting a seat is another part of the ritual. One way is the five-concert ballot, which requires fans to attend at least five other Proms concerts before applying for Last Night tickets. Other options include a smaller public ballot, whole-season passes and limited day-of standing returns.

title: Cadini di Misurina, Dolomites, Veneto, Italy
caption: A reef above its station
description: The image captures the jagged skyline of Cadini di Misurina at sunrise in Veneto, northeastern Italy. Visitors heading towards nearby Tre Cime di Lavaredo often come for the famous route only to find their attention hijacked by the Cadini. Part of the Dolomites, these needle-like peaks reaching more than 2,800 metres at their highest point seem sculpted for drama. The twist? They started out as ancient coral reefs.
